key_insight: IRPO integrates a reinforcement-learning reformulation with the Bradley–Terry generative reward model to remove the costly O(n^2) pairwise-comparison bottleneck, enabling scalable reward estimation for larger candidate sets.
problem_solved: Pairwise generative reward models (GRMs) used with RL methods like GRPO require O(n^2) comparisons to obtain relative scores, creating a severe computational bottleneck that prevents scaling to many candidates or frequent online updates.
method: Introduce IRPO: an RL-driven reformulation that learns implicit preferences compatible with the Bradley–Terry model without enumerating all pairwise comparisons.
Integrate IRPO into Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) to estimate relative rewards with far fewer comparisons and enable end-to-end training.
Optimize for training/inference efficiency (reduced compute and memory) while preserving GRM interpretability and refinability via RL.
impact: IRPO makes generative reward models practical at scale, lowering compute and latency for preference/ranking tasks (e.g., LLM preference learning, response ranking) and enabling faster iteration and deployment of reward-driven systems.
